concept.name: Moving average envelope
concept.definition: Parallel bands set a fixed percentage above and below a simple or exponential moving average, creating a constant-width channel used for trend confirmation and, in flat markets, as overbought/oversold references.
concept.intuition: Unlike volatility-adaptive bands, the percentage offset never changes, so a touch of the envelope always means 'price is x% stretched from its average.'
concept.mechanics: Upper = MA x (1 + p), Lower = MA x (1 - p), e.g., a 20-day SMA with p = 2.5%. Parameters must be chosen per security volatility - indexes need narrow envelopes (2-3%), volatile stocks wide ones (5-10%).
concept.formula: Upper = MA(n) x (1 + p); Lower = MA(n) x (1 - p); e.g., MA = SMA(20), p = 0.025.
concept.failure_modes: The fixed width does not adapt: too narrow in volatility expansions (constant false breaks) and too wide in quiet periods (no signals at all); it also inherits the base average's lag.
concept.misconceptions: Envelope breaks in a strong trend are signs of strength, not fade setups; overbought/oversold logic applies mainly when the trend is flat.
concept.example: A 20-day SMA of 40 with 2.5% envelopes plots the upper band at 41.0 and the lower at 39.0.
